privacy.title: Protection of personal data

sections.heading: Collection and processing
sections.body:
When you visit our website, you may be asked to provide personal information that relates to you (name, surname, occupation, e-mail address, postal address, etc.) so that we can provide our services as effectively as possible. Any personal data you submit on our website are kept exclusively for purposes related to your transactions with us, improving the services provided, and ensuring the operation of the relevant service, and may not be used by any third party (except where provided by law to the competent authorities only).

In any case, the employees who have access to your personal data are specifically designated, and access by unauthorised persons to your personal data is prohibited. Every reasonable measure has been taken to secure your data. In some cases your personal details may also be disclosed to partner companies, in order to support, promote and carry out your transactional relationship with us, but always under conditions that fully ensure that your personal data are not subject to any unlawful processing.

sections.heading: Your rights
sections.body: At any time, the user retains the right to be informed of, or to object to, further processing of their data in accordance with the applicable legislation on the protection of personal data, and has the following rights:

sections.heading: Access and information
sections.body: You have the right to obtain information about which data we have collected, for what purpose we collected it, and for how long we will retain it.

sections.heading: Rectification
sections.body: You have the right to ask us to correct any inaccurate information about you or to complete further information about you.

sections.heading: Restriction of and objection to processing
sections.body: You have the right to ask us to restrict or even to stop processing your personal data if you contest the accuracy of the information we hold about you, if you find that we are processing your data unlawfully, or if you no longer wish to receive promotional messages about our products and services.

sections.heading: Data portability
sections.body: You have the right to ask us to transfer your personal data to another organisation for you.

sections.heading: Erasure
sections.body: Finally, you have the right to ask us in writing to erase your personal data when they are no longer necessary in relation to the purposes for which they were collected, if you wish to withdraw your consent to this processing, and if your data have been unlawfully processed in breach of the regulation on the protection of personal data.

sections.heading: How to exercise your rights
sections.body: If you wish to exercise these rights, please contact us by email at hdaniel@otenet.gr

sections.heading: Agreement
sections.body: By using Mostro.gr you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, please do not use the website.

sections.heading: Use of the website
sections.body: You may use the site for lawful, personal, or internal business purposes related to learning about our products and contacting us. Do not attempt to disrupt the site, probe for vulnerabilities, or scrape it in a way that harms performance.

sections.heading: Information about products
sections.body: Specifications, images, and descriptions are for general information. They may change without notice. A sale is governed solely by the written agreement between you and us, not by this website alone.

sections.heading: Intellectual property
sections.body: Content on this site (text, images, branding) is owned by us or used with permission. You may not copy or reuse it for commercial purposes without our consent.

sections.heading: Limitation of liability
sections.body: The site is provided “as is” to the extent permitted by law. We are not liable for indirect loss or for issues caused by third-party services or links you follow from the site.

sections.heading: Governing law
sections.body: Where mandatory consumer law does not say otherwise, any dispute shall be subject to the courts of Greece.

sections.heading: Contact
sections.body: Questions about these terms: Info@mostro.gr or the contact details on our Contact page.

sections.heading: What are cookies?
sections.body: Cookies are small text files that are stored in your browser while you browse the internet. Their purpose is to tell the website you are visiting about your previous activity. They usually store information such as your username and password so that when you visit the same site later, it can “remember” you and you do not need to log in again.

sections.heading: Cookie categories
sections.body:
1) Strictly necessary cookies

These allow core site functions to run, such as adding products to the cart, online payment, and saving products to a wish list. Without these strictly necessary cookies, the smooth running of the e‑shop and your personal browsing experience are reduced, because basic e‑commerce functions do not work properly.

2) Performance cookies

Performance cookies collect information about how visitors use the website. They let us see which pages are visited most often, or show us whether visitors run into problems while browsing. These cookies do not collect information that identifies the visitor.

3) Functionality and analytics cookies

These cookies “remember” your preferences while you browse our site so we can suggest suitable products based on your needs. They also let us assess how effective different features of our site are.

4) Advertising cookies

These cookies are used to deliver ads that are more relevant to you and your interests. They are also used to send targeted advertising or offers in order to limit bulk, unwanted and pointless advertising messages. They also help us measure the effectiveness of advertising campaigns.

sections.heading: How you can disable cookies
sections.body:
You can set your browser to block or warn you about these cookies, but some parts of the website will not work correctly.

If you use Internet Explorer:

From the menu, choose “Tools”, then “Internet Options”.
Click the “Privacy” tab.
Choose the setting that suits you.

If you use Google Chrome:

Choose “Settings”, then “Advanced”.
Under “Privacy and security”, click “Content settings”.
Click “Cookies”.

If you use Safari:

Choose “Preferences”, then “Privacy”.
Click “Remove all website data”.

If you use Mozilla Firefox:

From the menu, choose “Tools”, then “Options”.
Click the “Privacy” icon.
Find the “cookies” menu and choose the relevant options.

Finally, if you use Opera 6.0:

From the menu, choose “Files”, then “Preferences”.
Click “Privacy”.
